aiAnalysis.rootCause: The login submission completed, but the test could not detect any authenticated-user indicator afterward. The most likely cause is that the app either did not finish the sign-in redirect/state update or the post-login UI changed and no longer exposes any of the expected selectors ([data-user], .user-menu, .avatar, #profile, .logout-btn, or logout buttons).
aiAnalysis.suggestion: Verify that authentication actually succeeds in the app after submit, then update the smoke test to wait for a reliable post-login signal that matches the current UI. If the UI is correct, add a dedicated auth assertion or test id for a stable authenticated-state marker.

aiInsights: The test run failed with 0 of 1 cases passing, resulting in a Quality Score of 39/100. That score indicates the build is well below an acceptable quality threshold and is not ready for release or further downstream validation. The single failure should be treated as a blocking issue until the underlying defect is identified and resolved.
The run shows a single point of failure concentrated in authentication verification, so coverage is narrow and the failure is easy to localize.
The test depends on multiple brittle CSS/text selectors for post-login detection, which increases maintenance risk when the UI changes.
The presence of a saved browser state suggests the test reached the auth flow, but the absence of a user indicator implies either a real login issue or a selector mismatch after a UI transition.
This failure is more consistent with a product or selector regression than with a broad environment outage.
Improving reliability would require a stable authenticated-state test id and explicit waits/assertions for the post-login route or session state.
